title: Money in on a card lowers what is owed; only a refund gives money back to a budget line (AS7, F5, O)
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027: the bank holds 300,000, of which Food 30,000 and Free to spend 50,000 (typed). A card closes on the 15th and is paid in full on the 10th of the next month from the bank (moved later); its last statement, closed 15 Dec 2026, was paid and nothing is owed. Pay of 250,000 on the 25th (moved earlier). Wed 6 Jan: 20,000 of food on the card. Fri 8 Jan: a shop refunds 3,000 to the card, and the person gives it back to Food. Mon 11 Jan: 5,000 of cashback is credited to the card. Tue 12 Jan: a friend pays 2,000 for a shared dinner straight onto the card, and the person names Food on it; it is money in, not a refund. Every amount is made up.

events.note: a friend's share of a dinner, paid onto the card; money in, not a refund

asks.question: owed_now
asks.why: 20,000 (food on the card, Wed 6 Jan) - 3,000 (refund, Fri 8 Jan) - 5,000 (cashback, money in, Mon 11 Jan) - 2,000 (a friend's money in, Tue 12 Jan) = 10,000
asks.note: Money in on a card lowers what is owed, refund or not [AS7].

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.why: 300,000 (bank today) - 13,000 (Food left: 30,000 less the 20,000 bought on the card plus the 3,000 refund given back to it; the friend's 2,000 names Food but is not a refund, so it gives nothing back [AS7]) = 287,000
